# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`

1137	### D.18 Thermal drift (the cold-room invariant)
1138	
1139	The `thermal_drift` formula is defined as (a lint and report formula, harness-side; the natural logarithm is forbidden on the sim path and nothing hashed depends on it):
1140	
1141	`tau_steps = floor(100 x V x C_TILE / (K_HULL x S_ext))` = `floor(12000 x V / S_ext)` at the defaults ; `t_cross_min = tau_steps x ln((T0 - T_AMB_MC) / (ONSET_MC - T_AMB_MC)) / 600` for `T0 > ONSET_MC` ; `COLD_ROOM_DRIFT iff t_cross_min < COLD_ROOM_SAFE_MIN` (sealed, unheated, doors closed) ; `COLD_ROOM_UNDECLARED iff T0 <= ONSET_MC and the room is not the declared lethal room`
1142	
1143	**Variables:**
1144	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
1145	|---|---|---|---|---|
1146	| `V` | int tiles | 4 to 200 | LY D.3 | Room volume |
1147	| `S_ext` | int tiles | 1 to 80 | DA-7 `exposed_tiles` (`THERMAL_INPUT_MISSING` if absent) | Hull tiles exposed |
1148	| `C_TILE`, `K_HULL` | int | 3000 / 25 | LSG D.7 | Thermal mass per tile (dJ per C) and hull conductance |
1149	| `T0` | int mC | authored | C.1 to C.3 | Initial room temperature |
1150	| `T_AMB_MC` | int mC | -30000 | LSG (R14; MVP exterior sink) | Exterior temperature |
1151	| `ONSET_MC` | int mC | -20000 | SE D.4 (`COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC` -15000 less `INSUL_MC` 5000 `[PLACEHOLDER: Suit]`) | Shifted cold onset, at full suit integrity (at or above `SUIT_LEAK_HP`); a leaking suit moves the onset toward `COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC` -15000 (SE-21), and `COLD_ROOM_DRIFT` also prints the -15000 projection |
1152	| `COLD_ROOM_SAFE_MIN` | int min | 25 (range 20 to 60) | Authoring knob (Checkpoint rulings Q7; not registry) | Required loaded minutes above the onset. Closed doors let unheated rooms cool to COOL or FROST within 20 to 30 minutes, and that is the intended consequence of closed-door play, not a warning: default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |

I'm still untangling whether "no cell of any door assembly" refers only to the floor region or the whole structural assembly including the pocket, since the approach-clear requirement for the door (a clear floor cell in front of it) muddies whether that counts as "assembly" too. This really is the core ambiguity that remains unresolved.

Running the numbers more carefully: the route distance past the door centre (54 to 252 px toward the dock) translates to y = 1026 down to 828, and the door assembly extent [936,1128) overlaps that range on [936,1026] — so a literal lint check would actually fire a violation here. The proposal's own text only addresses clearance relative to the dock door, staying silent about whether its own door's assembly counts against the same rule.

I'm leaning toward resolving this as RECOMMENDED severity rather than blocking, with a concrete fix: redefine the window as corridor floor cells not occupied by any door's leaf swing, approach, or pocket cells, exempting the machine door's own pocket region near the centre — or alternatively, clarify that "door assembly" refers to the leaf/jamb rect in the wall plane rather than corridor floor cells, which would resolve the conflict entirely.

findings.section: DA-46; DA-40 DOCK_GLOW_LUMINANCE (L556); Tuning Knobs DOCK_GLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_PM (L1483); Visual/Audio L1580; AC-DA-145
findings.finding: Third carry (G3). The ERROR lint DOCK_GLOW_LUMINANCE caps the glow at 250 permille of the residual lamp's output_pm. The Emitter owns DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM, which defaults to 500 with a floor of 300 (I-DOCK C2, registry range 300-800). With the residual lamp at or near full output, the ratio at the owner's default is about 500, so the ERROR fires on shipped templates. AC-DA-144 (console lit) and AC-DA-145 (ratio <= 250) cannot both pass. Under G1 the Emitter wins, so implementation is unambiguous, but the Authoring knob and its 100-500 range are wrong.
findings.fix: Conform the knob to the owner: derive the cap as ratio >= base_pm / residual output_pm (500 or higher), or state the lint against the Emitter's DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM directly and drop the independent 250. Make the knob range's lower bound at least 300 permille of the lamp's output at the Emitter default. Update L653, L1480-1483, L1580 and AC-DA-145 together, then grep for '250 permille'.

findings.section: DA-46 Placement; DA-41 / DA-40 SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT (L566); OQ-DA-46; AC-DA-144

E1 creates a DOCK_STATUS glow OFF whatever the authoring says, and E10 set_dock_status (called by Web Map in the pod_at apply) turns it on only in the room where the pod parks. AC-DA-144 asserts every console in all three dock rooms is lit by the glow alone. A correct build can never pass that, because the other two rooms' glows are off.
findings.fix: Rewrite DA-46 so the glow is authored as subkind DOCK_STATUS, with no switch_on and no hard-coded node_ref list; BOOT keys on the subkind. Close OQ-DA-46. Rewrite AC-DA-144: 'for the dock room where pod_at holds the pod (E10 on), every CONSOLE anchor within 24 px is lit by the glow alone with the bus dead, every other emitter dark and the beam off; the consoles in the other two dock rooms are dark.'

findings.section: D.18 tell lead (L1173); AC-DA-133; B timeline table (L1254)
findings.finding: G4 off-by-one in an exact oracle. The formula is t_tell_steps = ceil(tau x ln(...)). With tau 22,857, T_eq_hot 68,286 and HEAT_TELL_STEP_MC 44,700, I get 22,857 x ln(26,286 / 23,586) = 2,477.31, so the ceiling is 2,478. The GDD and AC-DA-133 assert 2,477 and lead 293 (29.3 s, 1,758 ticks). The correct lead is 292 (29.2 s, 1,752 ticks), and the margin over the floor is 192, not 193. The onset 2,770 and the 44,897 / 44,898 boundary check out (lead 100 / 99). A correct build fails the exact AC.
findings.fix: Change t_tell_steps to 2,478, lead_steps to 292 (29.2 s), the margin to 192, and the timeline row to 2,478 after V12 (3,078 B-loaded). Update AC-DA-133 to match.

findings.section: DA-40 lint tranches (L639); DWELL_BUDGET_LOW; D.23; AC-DA-162; OQ-DA-56
findings.finding: The tranche rule says a tranche is complete when its rows run clean on the shipped templates. DWELL_BUDGET_LOW is a T2 ERROR that is red on the shipped plan by design (104 s vs 190 s), so T2 can never complete, and a later tranche is told not to block an earlier one. The same sequencing hole applies to DOCK_GLOW_LUMINANCE at the owner's default.
findings.fix: Declare DWELL_BUDGET_LOW WARN until OQ-DA-56 closes (the same pattern as DECISION_REACH_MISSING), then promote it to ERROR in T2. Or list known-red rows as exempt from the tranche-complete test. AC-DA-162 then passes on the rule fixtures (189 fires, 190 does not) and the shipped-plan check stays BLOCKED.

That is Boarding's labelled pre-ruling anchor, which matches Derelict's plan of record (204 px) only until the plan-of-record switch. Under G1 Boarding owns the figure.
findings.fix: State both: 'Boarding D.4 margin_pm = 250 at today's 204 px plan, 266 at the DA-48 proposal (228 px, 582 ticks)', and key AC-DA-138 to the plan of record in force.

findings.section: AC-DA-77; Tuning Knobs A_BUS_BATTERY_DJ (L1468); AC-DA-155; THAW_REACHABLE
findings.finding: AC-DA-77 names 'a larger b_a2 (range to 2,160,000)' as the recovery lever. The knob ceiling is 1,950,000, and above 1,956,599 THAW_REACHABLE (ERROR) fires on the pooled battery (AC-DA-155 fails at 1,960,000). The stated recovery would break the build.
findings.fix: Rewrite as 'a larger b_a2 up to the 1,950,000 ceiling (a margin of at most 330 steps at the full-bus load of 1,600 W: 1,950,000 / 1,600 = 1,218 steps)', or a lower PUMP_TELL_MIN_STEPS.

findings.section: AC-DA-122 and AC-DA-121 (R12)
findings.finding: AC-DA-122 prints 'at most 16.6 ms ... 33.3 ms ... within 90 % of each ceiling'. Those are two different pass lines (16.6 vs 14.9 ms), and R12 makes 90 % binding. AC-DA-121 applies the frame-ceiling 90 % clause ('P99 within 90 % of the machine's ceiling') to a per-tick simulation budget of STEP_BUDGET_MS 4, which is a different quantity.
findings.fix: AC-DA-122: 'P99 frame time <= 14.9 ms on RM-DESKTOP and <= 30.0 ms on RM-DECK'. AC-DA-121: 'P99 simulation time per tick <= STEP_BUDGET_MS 4 on each machine; the frame ceiling is not the pass line'.

findings.section: AC-DA-96; AC-DA-100
findings.finding: Two ACs are untestable or inject no violation. AC-DA-96 requires 'zero leaked RefCounted handles', and gdUnit4 reports orphan nodes, not RefCounted leaks. findings.fix: AC-DA-96: 'zero orphan nodes (gdUnit4 orphan detection) and the suite's RefCounted object count, read through Performance.get_monitor(OBJECT_COUNT), is unchanged before and after the run'. findings.section: D.18 tell lead (L1173); AC-DA-133; B timeline table (L1254)
findings.finding: G4 off-by-one in an exact oracle. The formula is t_tell_steps = ceil(tau x ln(...)). With tau 22,857, T_eq_hot 68,286 and HEAT_TELL_STEP_MC 44,700, I get 22,857 x ln(26,286 / 23,586) = 2,477.31, so the ceiling is 2,478. The GDD and AC-DA-133 assert 2,477 and lead 293 (29.3 s, 1,758 ticks). The correct lead is 292 (29.2 s, 1,752 ticks), and the margin over the floor is 192, not 193. The onset 2,770 and the 44,897 / 44,898 boundary check out (lead 100 / 99). A correct build fails the exact AC.
findings.fix: Change t_tell_steps to 2,478, lead_steps to 292 (29.2 s), the margin to 192, and the timeline row to 2,478 after V12 (3,078 B-loaded). Update AC-DA-133 to match.

findings.section: DA-40 lint tranches (L639); DWELL_BUDGET_LOW; D.23; AC-DA-162; OQ-DA-56
findings.finding: The tranche rule says a tranche is complete when its rows run clean on the shipped templates. DWELL_BUDGET_LOW is a T2 ERROR that is red on the shipped plan by design (104 s vs 190 s), so T2 can never complete, and a later tranche is told not to block an earlier one. The same sequencing hole applies to DOCK_GLOW_LUMINANCE at the owner's default.
findings.fix: Declare DWELL_BUDGET_LOW WARN until OQ-DA-56 closes (the same pattern as DECISION_REACH_MISSING), then promote it to ERROR in T2. Or list known-red rows as exempt from the tranche-complete test. AC-DA-162 then passes on the rule fixtures (189 fires, 190 does not) and the shipped-plan check stays BLOCKED.
